content.title: About
content.content: Pork ham hocks (smoked) are cuts from the front leg of a pig, usually with the bone attached, that undergo curing and smoking. They have a rich aroma, firm texture, and a slightly sweet, smoky flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ham hocks are a staple in traditional Russian dishes such as rassolnik and hearty broths.
Smoking preserves the meat by reducing moisture and creating antimicrobial compounds.
In many regions the hocks are served cold, thinly sliced as an appetizer.
High collagen content makes them a good source of gelatin when slow‑cooked.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Ham hocks provide high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which helps prevent anemia.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12, B6 and niacin, important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides zinc and phosphorus, supporting immune health and bone strength.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Smoked hocks are often heavily salted, which can raise blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Nitrites and nitrates
items.content: Smoking may introduce nitrite compounds, which are considered potentially harmful in large amounts.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Ham hocks contain saturated fats; people with high cholesterol should limit intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the hocks thinly for cold platters, add them to soups, stews, or braise with vegetables. Before cooking, trim excess fat and rinse to reduce excess salt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the hocks refrigerated at 0 °C–4 °C in an airtight package for 5–7 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C, where they retain quality for up to 3 months. Before use, check for off‑odors or discoloration, which indicate spoilage.

content.title: About
content.content: Cooked potato is boiled tubers of Solanum tuberosum that are widely used as a base for dishes, side‑courses, salads and purees. Boiling retains most of its nutrients, gives a soft texture and a neutral flavor that pairs well with many other ingredients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato is the fourth most produced food crop worldwide after cereals, rice and wheat.
Boiled potato retains about 80 % of its vitamin C, which degrades with prolonged storage.
Larger potato varieties generally require longer cooking times than smaller ones due to denser flesh.
Cooked potato is a staple in many diet plans because it is low‑calorie and high in fiber.
There are over 4 000 potato varieties, but only a small fraction are ideal for boiling.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Cooked potato provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Good source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance, blood pressure, and supports muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety and supports gut health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Boiled potato contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Provides vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: Green or sprouted potatoes may contain the toxic glycoalkaloid solanine; boiling does not completely eliminate it.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Cooked potato has a high glycemic index, which can cause rapid spikes in blood sugar.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: Nutrient loss with overcooking
items.content: Excessive boiling can reduce levels of vitamin C and some B‑vitamins.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked potato can be served as a side dish, added to salads, soups, casseroles, mashed, or used as a filling for pies. It can be diced, sliced, or pureed according to the recipe.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool boiled potatoes should be kept in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. Do not leave them at room temperature for more than 2 hours to prevent bacterial growth.

content.title: About
content.content: Home fries are pieces of boiled or baked potato that are pan‑fried until golden and crispy. They are a staple side dish in fast‑food restaurants, often served alongside burgers, steaks, and other main courses. The potatoes retain a tender interior while the exterior develops a satisfying crunch.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes are the world’s fourth most produced food crop after rice, wheat, and corn.
The term “home fries” is commonly used in the United States for diced or chunked potatoes cooked with the skin on.
Unlike classic French fries, home fries are usually made from larger pieces, preserving more nutrients.
Seasonings such as rosemary, paprika, garlic, or herbs are often added for extra flavor.
Many restaurants use a double‑fry method: a low‑heat first fry for softness, then a high‑heat second fry for crispness.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potatoes provide a high amount of potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Heat‑processing retains a portion of vitamin C, a powerful antioxidant.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Home fries contain slowly digestible carbs that give lasting satiety.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: When cooked with the skin, potatoes supply dietary fiber that benefits digestion.

items.title: Beta‑carotene
items.content: They contain provitamin A, which supports vision and immune health.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Frying adds significant fat, so portion control is important.

items.title: Trans fats from reused oil
items.content: Reusing oil can create trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Excessive salting can raise blood pressure; use salt sparingly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Home fries are served hot as a side dish with meat entrees, in burgers, or as a snack with dips such as ketchup, mayo, or ranch. They can be topped with fresh herbs, cheese, or your favorite seasonings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked home fries are best enjoyed immediately. If needed, store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days and reheat in the oven to restore crispness.

content.title: About
content.content: Whopper Jr is a smaller burger from Burger King, featuring a 100 % beef patty, fresh vegetables (lettuce, tomato, pickles, onion), Whopper sauce, mayonnaise, and a sesame seed bun. Served hot and cooked on the grill.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Whopper Jr was introduced in the 1990s as a more affordable version of the classic Whopper.
The burger is often featured in promotional campaigns and limited‑time releases, such as double sauce or plant‑based patty versions.
In some markets the Whopper Jr can be ordered without onions upon request.
Its portion size targets children and teens, but it is also popular among adults as a light snack.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef and the bun supply B12, B6, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Beef is a good source of heme iron, which aids normal blood formation.

items.title: High calories and saturated fat
items.content: Despite its smaller size, the burger contains saturated fats and calories that can contribute to weight gain if eaten frequently.

items.title: Gluten and dairy allergens
items.content: The bun and sauces may contain gluten and dairy ingredients that can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Sauces and pickles add a notable amount of salt, which is undesirable for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Whopper Jr is typically served in its branded wrapper. It is eaten by hand, often accompanied by fries or a drink. Customizations such as no onion or sauce swaps are available.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The burger should be consumed immediately after preparation. If needed, keep it refrigerated for no more than 2 hours, then reheat in a microwave or on a grill before eating.
